messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Randomized incomplete block designs?
parts:
Without knowing the particulars of your setup, I can say that the sample() function is your friend. 

Assuming you will have balanced incomplete blocks (within block, every treatment occurs the same number of times): You can set up your treatments as the "x" and with replace = FALSE, it will randomly assign your treatments to each spot available. Just repeat by looping through your blocks, changing the "x" argument according to the number of available spots in each block (i.e. if you have 2 treatments (A & B), and 4 spots in block 1, sample(rep(c("A","B"), 2), replace = FALSE), if you have 2 spots in block 2, sample(rep(c("A","B"), 1), replace = FALSE)).  

Things can get a fair bit messier if you have an unbalanced design. In these cases, it can make sense to use some kind of stratified sampling to ensure every treatment occurs at least once in each block. 

As far as analysis of messy designs, my go-to reference is:

http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/AOS259.pdf

Hope that helps,

Matt
